extracted.intended_audience: school administrators, Title IX coordinators, higher-education legal counsel, and recipients of federal financial assistance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for school recipients on conducting Title IX grievance processes (investigations, evidence disclosure, notices, written determinations) while addressing interplay with FERPA and constitutional protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of constitutional rights / saving clause
rubrics_metrics.description: A catch-all saving clause clarifying that nothing in the final regulations requires a recipient to infringe upon any individual's rights protected under the First Amendment or the Due Process Clauses, or any other rights guaranteed by the U.S. Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not interpret these regulations to obligate private recipients to restrict speech or other behavior that the Federal government could not constitutionally restrict; citations include Peterson v. City of Greenville and Truax v. Raich. Inclusion of §106.6(d)(3) is intended to ensure constitutional rights are respected and does not imply fault by recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural due process: notice and meaningful opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural due process requires notice and a meaningful opportunity to respond; provisions such as §106.45(b)(5)(vi) (access to evidence) and §106.45(b)(5)(iv) (advisor of choice) help protect a party's procedural due process rights under the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must structure grievance processes to give parties timely notice of allegations and proceedings and a meaningful chance to rebut or respond; the Department is bound by the Constitution and cannot administer Title IX in a way that deprives due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to evidence directly related to the allegations (§106.45(b)(5)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide both parties an equal opportunity to inspect and review any evidence obtained as part of the investigation that is directly related to the allegations raised in a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department specifies that the recipient must send the evidence subject to inspection and review in an electronic format to each party and the party's advisor, if any. The recipient may also provide hard copies; the rules neither require nor prohibit providing hard copies. Evidence exchange is necessary to provide due process, though redaction of highly sensitive information may be appropriate in limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to an advisor of choice at all meetings (§106.45(b)(5)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are allowed to bring an advisor of their choice to all meetings in the Title IX proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This right protects party participation and fairness; evidence and communications to the party's advisor must follow the same disclosure rules as to the party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic delivery requirement for inspection materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department specifies that the recipient must send to each party and the party's advisor the evidence subject to inspection and review in an electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients retain discretion to also provide hard copies. The final regulation revision explicitly allows either electronic format or a hard copy, preserving flexibility for recipients and parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion over use of restrictive file-sharing platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may use, but are not required to use, file-sharing platforms that restrict parties and advisors from downloading or copying evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed a specific reference to such platforms from the final regulations to emphasize that use of such platforms is discretionary and not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion and Department enforcement on 'directly related' determination
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient has some discretion to determine whether evidence obtained as part of an investigation is directly related to allegations, but the Department enforces both Title IX and FERPA and may investigate complaints about failure to provide equal opportunity to inspect/review evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'directly related to' requirement aligns with FERPA's definition of education records. If a party complains the recipient withheld directly related evidence, the Department will investigate and determine compliance with §106.45(b)(5)(vi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment/medical/mental-health records: voluntary written consent required (§106.45(b)(5)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient cannot access, consider, disclose, or otherwise use a party's records made or maintained by a physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, or other recognized professional or paraprofessional acting in that capacity in connection with provision of treatment, unless the party provides voluntary, written consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the party is not an 'eligible student' as defined in 34 CFR 99.3, the recipient must obtain the voluntary, written consent of a parent. If consent is provided and such records are directly related to the allegations, the recipient must provide both parties equal opportunity to inspect and review them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) must not inhibit evidence/exchange or discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX does not require or prohibit NDAs, but any NDA must not restrict a party's ability to discuss the allegations under investigation or to gather and present relevant evidence under §106.45(b)(5)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any NDA must comply with all applicable laws; NDAs cannot preclude a party from participating fully in the grievance process or from exchanging evidence necessary for due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice requirement for investigative interviews, meetings, and hearings (§106.45(b)(5)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide written notice to a party whose participation is invited or expected of all hearings, investigative interviews, or other meetings with a party, with sufficient time for the party to prepare to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written notices may need to include identities of parties and witnesses where relevant for preparation. This provision parallels Clery Act regulatory notice requirements and is not interpreted to violate FERPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of written determination (§106.45(b)(7)(ii)(E))
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination must include any sanctions the recipient imposes on the respondent, and whether remedies designed to restore or preserve equal access will be provided to the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written determination should list measures insofar as they constitute sanctions, and should state whether remedies will be provided without disclosing details of complainant-specific remedies that do not directly affect the respondent. For overlapping measures (e.g., no-contact orders), list them as sanctions and note remedies will be provided, preserving complainant confidentiality where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of complainant's remedy details
rubrics_metrics.description: Details of remedies provided to a complainant remain part of the complainant's education record and are not the respondent's education record unless the remedy also imposes requirements on the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a remedy does not directly affect the respondent (e.g., changing complainant's housing), the written determination should simply state that remedies will be provided; the complainant communicates privately with the Title IX Coordinator about remedy details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with FERPA: interpret statutes to avoid conflict; Title IX may override FERPA in direct conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should interpret Title IX and FERPA to avoid conflicts. Where there is a direct conflict such that FERPA enforcement would interfere with Title IX's primary purpose, the Department's longstanding interpretation (and GEPA legislative history) is that Title IX overrides conflicting FERPA provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department continues its 2001 interpretation: FERPA applies in Title IX enforcement contexts, but Title IX requirements supersede FERPA where direct conflict exists. Recipients remain required to comply with all applicable laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA and Clery Act exceptions relevant to disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: FERPA contains provisions permitting disclosure, without prior written consent, to an alleged victim of a crime of violence or nonforcible sex offense of the final results of disciplinary proceedings (20 U.S.C. 1232g(b)(6)); the Clery Act and its regulations require institutions to provide results of proceedings including sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory provisions inform how disclosures can be made; the Department acknowledges §99.33(c) (FERPA redisclosure inapplicability where Clery applies) and that some disclosures are statutorily permitted even under FERPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' right to identities of other parties/witnesses when necessary for due process
rubrics_metrics.description: A party such as a complainant or respondent must know who the other parties in a formal complaint are in order to support or challenge the allegations, and written notices may include identities of witnesses and parties when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For recipients that are State actors, constitutional due process would require such disclosure; FERPA's definitions of education records do not preclude inspection of witness statements that are directly related to the student when information cannot be segregated without destroying meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient obligation to comply with state and other applicable laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with all applicable laws; the Department's regulations do not relieve recipients of obligations under state law (e.g., two-party consent recording laws, protections for IEPs/Section 504 plans) or other Federal statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters raised concerns that some state laws may limit production of certain recordings or records; recipients should consider state constraints when producing evidence and seek lawful ways to comply with both Title IX and other legal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal treatment of employee-respondents regarding access and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties, including employee-respondents, are entitled to the same procedural protections (access to relevant evidence, advisor rights, notice) afforded to student parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cannot interpret Title IX or FERPA to compel private schools to deprive employee-respondents of due process rights, including review of evidence directly related to allegations and ability to bring an advisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange of evidence may be uncomfortable but is necessary for due process; redaction limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing investigative reports and evidence may cause discomfort for complainants, but exchange is necessary to provide adequate due process to both parties; recipients may redact highly sensitive information but both parties need the ability to review evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients can consider redaction of narrowly tailored, highly sensitive details, or sanctions for unlawful public disclosure, but should ensure that redactions do not undermine a party's ability to challenge or defend allegations.
